claims.text: During layout a parent gives each child constraints: minimum and maximum width and height. LayoutBuilder calls its builder with the BoxConstraints its parent gives it, so the returned subtree can depend on the available size.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: ui/layout/constraints.md; API docs: LayoutBuilder

claims.text: ProductCatalog@stage-1: below maxWidth 600 it returns ListView.builder of ProductTile; otherwise GridView.builder with crossAxisCount = floor(maxWidth / 300) and mainAxisExtent 72 (each tile's height in a vertical grid), same ProductTile. ProductTile shows a product's name and price.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: product_catalog.dart:17-37, product_tile.dart; API docs: SliverGridDelegateWithFixedCrossAxisCount.mainAxisExtent

claims.text: At stage-1 no screen uses ProductCatalog; ProductListScreen still builds its own ListView (so the stretched rows are not yet fixed).

product_catalog_test.dart wraps ProductCatalog in MaterialApp/Scaffold/Center/SizedBox of width 360 or 900; at 360 it finds a ListView and no GridView, at 900 a GridView with two ProductTiles; the tests pass. pumpWidget builds the widget; expect + find.byType checks the tree.
Column counts from the code: 600 -> 2, 900 -> 3, 1250 -> 4; 599 and 360 -> ListView.
Deciding a layout from the whole app window's size gives the wrong answer when a widget gets only part of the window (e.g. a side panel); deciding from its constraints keeps working.

In flutter test the default test view is 800x600 logical pixels; Center passes loose constraints capped at it, so SizedBox(width: 900) is laid out 800 wide and LayoutBuilder sees maxWidth 800 (2 columns), while SizedBox(width: 360) gives 360.
claims.source_hint: flutter test probe on stage-1 (technical review); Flutter docs ui/layout/constraints.md
